1: Prepare|Cut the tomatoes into wedges and chop the scallion. Beat the eggs with one-third of the salt, the pepper, sesame oil and wine.
Scramble|Heat two-thirds of the cooking oil over medium heat. Stir the eggs into soft curds and transfer to a clean bowl.
Cook tomatoes|Add the remaining cooking oil, tomatoes and scallion. Stir-fry over high heat for 1 minute; add the sugar, remaining salt and measured water.
Finish|Return the eggs, cover and cook for 1–2 minutes until the tomatoes soften. Uncover and reduce the juices; ensure the egg is fully cooked before serving.
2: Prepare|Peel the potato and cut into fine, even matchsticks. Rinse away surface starch and drain well. Chop the chilies, scallions and garlic.
Flavor the oil|Warm the oil over medium heat with the Sichuan peppercorns. Remove the peppercorns when fragrant; briefly fry the chilies and garlic without scorching.
Stir-fry|Raise the heat and toss in the potato. Stir frequently until cooked but still crisp, adding the scallions toward the end.
Season|Add the vinegar, salt and black pepper to taste. Toss thoroughly and serve immediately.
3: Prepare|Remove the cabbage core, tear the leaves into bite-size pieces, wash and dry thoroughly. Crush and chop the garlic.
First batch|Heat two-thirds of the oil over high heat. Add half the garlic and cabbage. Let edges color briefly, then toss for 2–3 minutes; transfer out.
Second batch|Cook the remaining garlic and cabbage in the remaining oil. Use the measured water only if the pan becomes dry.
Finish|Return all cabbage to the pan. Add salt and sugar; toss until the leaves wilt and the ribs remain pleasantly firm.
4: Prepare|Cut the washed broccoli into florets and slice its peeled stem. Thinly slice the carrot. Mix the sauce, starch, one-ninth of the salt, pepper and measured water.
Blanch|Boil enough water to cover the vegetables and add the remaining salt. Cook broccoli for 1–1½ minutes, add carrot and cook for another minute. Drain.
Make sauce|Warm the oil over medium heat and briefly stir the crushed garlic until fragrant. Lower the heat and add the stirred sauce mixture.
Coat|When the sauce thickens, add the vegetables and toss until evenly glazed. Serve while tender-crisp.
5: Rehydrate|Cover the dried mushrooms with the measured hot water for about 30 minutes. Remove stems and reserve the sediment-free liquid. Wash and drain the bok choy.
Blanch greens|Boil water with two-fifths of the oil and the salt. Blanch bok choy about 40 seconds; cool briefly, drain and arrange on a plate.
Braise mushrooms|Heat remaining oil. Briefly fry garlic and mushrooms, add wine, reserved liquid, soy sauces, vegetarian oyster sauce, sugar, sesame oil and pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Thicken|Mix starch with a little cold water. Stir into the simmering sauce and cook about 1 minute until glossy. Spoon mushrooms and sauce over the greens.
6: Prepare|Cut the eggplant, potato and pepper into similar bite-size pieces. Salt the eggplant briefly and coat with half the starch. Mix the remaining starch with soy sauces, wine, pepper, sugar and water.
Cook separately|Heat most of the oil. Shallow-fry potatoes until a knife enters easily; remove. Fry peppers until blistered, then eggplant until soft. Drain each batch.
Make sauce|Retain a little cooking oil and briefly fry minced garlic and scallion. Stir the sauce again and pour it in.
Combine|Return the vegetables and toss until coated and the starch is cooked through. Serve promptly.
7: Prepare|Combine soy sauce, vinegar and sugar. Remove pepper stems and seeds; cut long peppers open. Chop the garlic.
Blister|Heat two-thirds of the oil over medium heat. Cook peppers, turning regularly, until softened with browned, wrinkled skins, about 15 minutes. Transfer out.
Season|Add remaining oil and garlic to the pan. Stir briefly until fragrant, then return the peppers.
Glaze|Pour in the sauce and toss for about 1 minute until it lightly coats the peppers. Lower the heat if the garlic begins to scorch.
8: Prepare|Cut eggplants into thick wedges. Stir water, wine, soy sauce, sugar, chili bean paste and starch together until smooth.
Start braise|Warm cooking oil in a wide covered skillet over medium heat. Stir minced garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds; add eggplant and sauce.
Simmer|Bring to a gentle boil, cover and cook about 15 minutes until the eggplant collapses and becomes tender.
Reduce|Uncover and simmer for 12–14 minutes, turning gently, until little liquid remains. Finish with sesame oil and sliced scallions.
9: Prepare|Pat tofu dry and cut into triangles. Slice garlic, ginger, carrot, pepper, scallions and bamboo shoots. Mix soy sauce, vinegar, vegetarian oyster sauce, sugar and three-quarters of the water. Mix starch with remaining water.
Fry tofu|Heat frying oil to 190°C / 375°F in a deep pan. Fry dry tofu in uncrowded batches until golden, then drain. Retain a thin film of oil.
Cook vegetables|Over medium heat, fry garlic, ginger, scallion whites and bean paste until fragrant. Add carrot, pepper and bamboo shoots; stir-fry.
Finish|Add tofu and sauce. Simmer until vegetables soften; stir in slurry until glossy. Finish with sesame oil and scallion greens.
10: Make dressing|Stir salt, sugar, sesame oil, soy sauce and vinegar together until dissolved. Finely chop the garlic and cilantro.
Prepare cucumbers|Wash and dry the cucumbers. Gently crack them with the flat side of a broad knife, keeping the blade away from your hands.
Cut and dress|Cut the cracked cucumbers into bite-size pieces. Toss thoroughly with the dressing and garlic.
Serve|Scatter over sesame seeds and cilantro. Serve promptly, or refrigerate until serving; keep utensils separate from those used for raw meat.
11: Prepare|Use properly rehydrated wood ears. Trim tough bases, rinse and tear into bite-size pieces. Follow the package soaking instructions; do not leave soaking at room temperature overnight.
Cook|Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. Boil the mushrooms for 3 minutes, then drain, cool with clean cold water and drain again.
Dress|Mix chopped garlic and chilies with vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil. Toss thoroughly with the mushrooms.
Serve|Add chopped scallions and refrigerate until chilled. Use clean utensils and keep the salad refrigerated until serving.
12: Marinate|Slice pork into fine strips. Mix with soy sauces, wine, five-spice, salt, starch and beaten egg white, then a little of the oil. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Prepare vegetables|Slice the green peppers into strips. Chop garlic and ginger; break the dried chilies into pieces.
Stir-fry|Heat most of the remaining oil over medium-high heat. Spread out the pork, sear briefly, then toss until cooked. Transfer to a clean plate.
Combine|Fry garlic, ginger, chilies and peppercorns in remaining oil. Add green peppers and stir until crisp-tender. Return pork, toss together and finish cooking fully.
13: Mix custard|Beat eggs with salt and the cup of warm water. Strain into a shallow heatproof bowl and skim away foam. Mix the starch with the separate measured water.
Steam|Place the bowl in a steamer over boiling water. Cover and steam gently for 10–12 minutes; continue until the center sets fully.
Cook topping|Heat oil in a skillet. Fry sliced scallion and ground pork, breaking up the meat. Stir in oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar, then the slurry.
Serve|Cook the pork topping until fully cooked and the sauce thickens. Spoon over the set custard and serve hot.
14: Parboil|Simmer the pork belly in the measured water for 30 minutes. Drain carefully, pat dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Discard the blanching liquid.
Brown|Warm oil in a lidded pan over medium heat. Brown the pork for about 2 minutes.
Braise|Add ginger, wine, star anise, peppercorns, chilies, stock, soy sauce, sugar and salt. Cover and maintain a gentle simmer for about 45 minutes.
Finish|Stir occasionally and continue until the pork is tender and the sauce glossy. Remove whole spices before serving.
15: Prepare|Pat chicken wings dry. Slice ginger, crush garlic and cut scallions into sections. Keep raw poultry away from ready-to-eat ingredients.
Brown|Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Brown wings on both sides; briefly stir in the aromatics.
Braise|Add soy sauces, sugar, wine and water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, turning occasionally.
Glaze|Check the thickest meat reaches 74°C / 165°F. Uncover and reduce the sauce until glossy, turning the wings to coat.
16: Rehydrate|Soak dried shiitakes and wood ears separately according to package instructions; allow up to an hour. Trim and rinse. Reserve clean, strained shiitake soaking liquid only.
Brown chicken|Heat oil over medium heat and fry ginger for 1 minute. Add chicken and brown for 3–5 minutes, then stir in the mushrooms for 2 minutes.
Braise|Add measured soaking liquid, wine, sugar and soy sauces. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer over low heat for 40–45 minutes.
Finish|Stir occasionally and add water if needed to prevent drying. Ensure chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F. Add scallion and cook until wilted.
17: Parboil beef|Cut brisket into 2 cm cubes. Cover with cold water, bring to a boil and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain and discard that water.
Simmer|Bring the measured fresh water to a boil with scallion segments, ginger slices, star anise and wine. Add beef and simmer, covered, about 1 hour until fork-tender.
Cook tomatoes|Chop tomatoes. Heat oil and briefly fry the measured chopped scallion and ginger. Add tomatoes and cook until pulpy.
Combine|Add tender beef and enough reserved broth to barely cover. Season to taste with salt, sugar and soy sauce. Reduce for 3–5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
18: Prepare|Use a professionally cleaned, scaled and gutted sea bass. Pat dry and place on a heatproof plate. Cut ginger into fine strips and slice scallions.
Set up steamer|Fill the lower pot to the steamer's recommended level and bring to a boil. Keep the fish plate above the water.
Steam|Scatter ginger over the fish, cover and steam about 10 minutes, extending as needed until the thickest flesh reaches 63°C / 145°F.
Finish|Warm sesame oil with garlic without smoking. Drizzle soy sauce and the fragrant oil over the fish; add scallions. Warn diners about bones.
19: Prepare|Have pork ribs cut into manageable pieces. Peel and seed the winter melon, then slice. Slice ginger and tie the scallion into a knot.
Blanch|Cover ribs with water and bring to a boil. Drain and discard the foamy liquid. Transfer ribs to a clean soup pot.
Simmer|Add ginger, scallion and fresh water to cover. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour.
Finish|Add winter melon and simmer about 15 minutes until translucent and the ribs are tender. Season with the measured salt and serve hot.
20: Prepare|Rehydrate laver seaweed according to the package directions, allowing about 15 minutes, then drain. Beat the eggs and chop scallion.
Make broth|Bring measured water, cooking oil and salt to a boil. Add the drained seaweed and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add eggs|Keep the soup gently simmering and pour in beaten egg in a thin stream. Leave briefly, then stir gently to create ribbons.
Finish|Add scallion to taste and continue until all egg is set and fully cooked. Serve the soup hot.
21: Prepare|Cube the tofu. Mix starch with measured water. Chop ginger, garlic and scallion; grind the Sichuan peppercorns.
Build flavor|Gently fry fresh and dried chilies in half the oil for about 5 minutes without scorching. Set aside. Heat remaining oil; fry ginger and garlic, then ground pork until cooked.
Make sauce|Add Sichuan pepper and bean paste; stir briefly, add stock and simmer. Stir in slurry and the reserved chili oil mixture.
Finish|Fold in tofu without crushing it. Simmer for 3–5 minutes, ensuring pork is fully cooked and the tofu hot throughout. Add scallion and serve.
22: Marinate|Dice chicken. Mix with the first starch and water measures, then sesame oil. Toast peanuts over low heat and set aside. Mix soy sauces, vinegar, wine, sugar and the remaining starch and water.
Start stir-fry|Heat cooking oil over medium-high heat. Briefly stir dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant, without burning them.
Cook chicken|Add chicken, followed by scallions, garlic and ginger. Stir-fry until the thickest pieces reach 74°C / 165°F.
Glaze|Stir the prepared sauce again and pour it in. Toss until thickened, then fold in peanuts and serve immediately.
23: Prepare|Cut pork into thin strips. Marinate with the first soy sauce, wine, starch, salt and water measures, then the teaspoon of oil. Combine the next seven sauce ingredients separately. Cut vegetables into fine strips.
Sear|Heat two-thirds of the cooking oil over high heat. Quickly sear pork and transfer out.
Cook vegetables|Add remaining oil, pickled chili, garlic and ginger. Stir until fragrant, then add carrot, wood ears and bamboo shoots; cook until tender-crisp.
Finish|Return pork. Stir in the sauce over lower heat until glossy and the pork fully cooked. Fold in chopped scallion and serve.
24: Simmer|Wash leeks thoroughly, separating dark leaves from pale parts. Simmer pork belly with ginger and dark leaves in measured water for 30–40 minutes until tender.
Chill and slice|Drain pork, discard cooking liquid and aromatics, and refrigerate promptly for at least 3 hours. Slice the cold pork thinly.
Render|Heat oil over medium-high heat. Stir-fry pork for 2–4 minutes until lightly browned; add black beans. Fry chili bean paste and sweet bean sauce in the rendered fat.
Finish|Add sliced pale leeks, dark soy sauce and sugar. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until leeks soften and the pork is thoroughly reheated.
25: Marinate fish|Slice boneless catfish about 1 cm thick. Coat with egg white, starch, two-thirds of the salt and half the pepper. Refrigerate while preparing the vegetables.
Build broth|Use half the oil to fry scallion whites, garlic, ginger and dried chilies. Add mustard greens and pickled peppers, stir briefly, then add wine, stock, sugar and remaining seasoning.
Poach|Simmer broth for 3–5 minutes. Move greens to a serving bowl. Gently poach separated fish slices in batches until the thickest reach 63°C / 145°F; transfer to the bowl with broth.
Finish|Warm remaining oil with Sichuan pepper and scallion greens until fragrant, without smoking. Spoon carefully over the fish and serve hot.
26: Marinate|Slice pork thinly. Mix with egg white, starch, wine, soy sauce and 4 g of the base salt measure. Prepare sprouts and chop scallions and garlic.
Cook sprouts|Stir-fry sprouts in 20 mL oil with 2 g salt until cooked through. Put in a deep heatproof serving bowl.
Poach pork|Fry bean paste in a little oil, add water and remaining base salt, then boil. Add pork slices separately and gently simmer until fully cooked. Pour over sprouts.
Finish|Top with chili powder, Sichuan pepper powder, garlic and scallions. Warm the remaining 30 mL oil until hot but not smoking; carefully spoon over the aromatics.
27: Prepare|Have a fishmonger split and clean the carp head, removing gills. Pat dry. Marinate with wine, soy sauce, pepper and half the ginger for 15 minutes.
Arrange|Place scallion whites and remaining ginger on a rimmed heatproof plate. Add the fish head and spread chopped salted chilies and minced garlic over it.
Steam|Set over boiling water, cover and steam for 12–15 minutes, extending until the thickest flesh reaches 63°C / 145°F.
Finish|Top with scallion greens and sesame oil. Warm cooking oil without smoking and spoon carefully over the scallions. Serve with attention to bones.
28: Prepare|Thinly slice skinless pork belly. Cut chili peppers into small pieces, crush garlic and rinse black beans.
Render pork|Heat oil over medium heat and fry the pork until lightly browned and some fat renders. Transfer meat out, retaining the fat.
Cook peppers|Raise the heat and stir-fry chili peppers and garlic until softened with some browned edges.
Combine|Return pork with black beans and both soy sauces. Toss until fully cooked and evenly seasoned, then serve hot.
29: Prepare|Remove chicken packaging and giblets without washing raw poultry. Use a pot large enough for the bird and enough water to submerge it. Add whole scallions and ginger slices; bring to a boil.
Poach|Carefully lower in chicken. Return to a simmer and maintain gentle heat, allowing roughly 35–45 minutes according to size. Check breast and inner thigh reach 74°C / 165°F.
Make dip|Finely mince the separate scallion and ginger measures. Mix with cooking oil and salt to taste.
Serve|Lift chicken out safely and rest before portioning with clean tools. Serve with the ginger-scallion dip. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.
30: Make filling|Combine minced pork, minced raw shrimp, finely chopped ginger, the half scallion, handful of cilantro, the smaller soy sauce measure, wine, sugar, pepper and one tablespoon starch.
Stuff tofu|Cut tofu into thick squares. Scoop small hollows, dust with the remaining starch and fill; do not overfill.
Steam|Arrange on a rimmed heatproof plate. Steam over boiling water for about 10 minutes, extending until filling reaches 72°C / 160°F.
Finish|Add sliced scallion, cilantro and remaining soy sauce. Warm oil until hot but not smoking and drizzle carefully over the garnish. Serve hot.
31: Marinate|Mix ginger juice from the smaller ginger measure with soy sauce, wine, sand ginger, five-spice and measured salt. Rub over chicken and refrigerate for 3 hours with half the scallions in its cavity.
Prepare salt bed|Wrap chicken securely in two crossed sheets of food-safe baking parchment and tie with kitchen string. Heat coarse rock salt in an oven at 220°C / 428°F for 30 minutes.

Bake|Using mitts, arrange a salt base in an oven-safe casserole, add wrapped chicken and cover completely with remaining hot salt. Cover and bake 75 minutes; verify chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F, then rest 10 minutes.
Serve|Remove parchment and discard baking salt. Combine remaining minced ginger, scallions, oil, sugar and seasoning salt for a separate dip. Do not eat or reuse the salt bed.
32: Prepare|Use fresh, commercially shucked oysters. Drain according to supplier instructions and check for shell fragments. Beat eggs and chop garlic chives.
Mix|Gently coat oysters in sweet potato starch and a little salt to taste; their retained moisture should make a light coating, not a watery batter.
Pan-fry|Heat oil in a flat skillet, then lower heat. Spread oysters in an even layer and cook until firm and cooked through, turning carefully if needed.
Add eggs|Pour beaten eggs around the oysters and sprinkle on chives. Cook until the egg is fully set; turn in portions as necessary. Serve immediately.
33: Prepare|Slice pressed tofu into very fine strips. Slice rehydrated shiitakes and ham; shred the cooked chicken. Rinse dried shrimp.
Blanch|Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add tofu strips, return to the boil, then drain and rinse to remove excess beany flavor.
Simmer|Bring chicken stock and dried shrimp to a boil. Add tofu, mushrooms, ham and cooked chicken; simmer gently for about 10 minutes.
Season|Add the measured salt gradually, using less if the stock is already salty. Add white pepper to taste. Ensure all reheated ingredients are piping hot and serve.
34: Mix|Combine pork, minced ginger and scallion, egg, breadcrumbs, first wine and soy sauce measures, oyster sauce, pepper, five-spice, starch and first water measure. Beat in one direction for 10 minutes; add minced water chestnuts and mix 5 minutes.
Brown|Shape equal meatballs. Fry in a deep pan at 175°C / 350°F until the outside sets and browns; drain. This does not finish cooking them.

Braise|Fry remaining ginger and scallion whites in the separate tablespoon oil. Dissolve sugar, then add remaining wine, soy sauces, oyster sauce and braising water. Add meatballs, cover and simmer 12–15 minutes; verify centers reach 72°C / 160°F.
Glaze|Combine final starch and water, stir into sauce, then add sesame oil and scallion greens. Coat the meatballs and serve.
35: Prepare|Have the whole carp scaled, gutted and cleaned professionally. Make shallow diagonal cuts in the thick flesh. Prepare a wide pan that holds it safely.
Poach|Boil measured water with ginger and scallion, lower in fish and reduce to a bare simmer. Cook about 8–10 minutes, extending until thickest flesh reaches 63°C / 145°F. Lift onto a platter.
Make glaze|Retain 120 mL poaching liquid. Add vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and pepper. Mix starch with wine; stir just enough into the simmering liquid to make a light glossy glaze.
Serve|Adjust salt only after tasting the sauce, pour over the fish and serve immediately. Watch carefully for bones.
36: Prepare|Separate pork ribs into individual pieces. Put measured water, both soy sauces, vinegar, wine and rock sugar into a wide lidded pot.
Dissolve|Heat over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add ribs and distribute evenly through the liquid.
Braise|Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for about 45 minutes, stirring and turning ribs occasionally.
Finish|Continue until ribs are tender and sauce coats them. If meat becomes tender before the sauce thickens, remove it briefly while reducing the liquid, then return to coat.
37: Marinate|Cut pork into finger-size strips. Mix with wine, soy sauce, oyster sauce, salt, pepper and beaten egg. Refrigerate for at least 20 minutes. Combine ketchup, vinegar, sugar and water separately.
Coat|Cover each pork strip in starch. Keep the coated pieces separate while heating frying oil in a deep, heavy pan.
Fry|Fry in small batches at 160°C / 320°F until the coating sets and meat cooks through. Drain; briefly fry again at 200°C / 392°F for about 40 seconds to crisp.
Glaze|Simmer the prepared sauce in a clean pan until bubbling. Toss in the pork just long enough to coat and serve immediately.
38: Prepare|Buy refrigerated, commercially pre-fermented mandarin fish from a traceable supplier and follow its label. Do not ferment fish at home. Prepare garlic, ginger, scallions and red chili.
Sear|Pat fish dry as directed by the supplier. Heat enough oil to film a skillet and fry gently on both sides until the skin sets; transfer out.

Braise|Briefly fry ginger, garlic and chili with bean paste to taste. Return fish and add hot water to cover. Simmer for 15–20 minutes, following any longer label cooking requirement and verifying thickest flesh reaches 63°C / 145°F.
Finish|Taste the sauce before adding sugar or soy sauces; the prepared fish is already salty. Reduce gently, add scallions and serve, watching for bones.
39: Blanch ribs|Cover ribs with cold water, bring just to a simmer, then drain. Discard the blanching water.
Prepare roots|Wash and peel lotus root, cleaning dirt from the holes. Slice 6–12 mm thick. Slice ginger and lightly crush garlic.
Simmer|Combine ribs, lotus root, goji berries, ginger, garlic, measured water and salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for at least 30 minutes.
Finish|Continue until the ribs and lotus root reach the tenderness you prefer. Adjust seasoning cautiously if the broth has reduced and serve hot.
40: Prepare pork|Slice pork 3 mm thick. Soak with baking soda and cold water for 10 minutes, rinse and drain thoroughly. Marinate with half the soy sauce, wine and salt. Mix starch with the measured water and coat pork.
Make sauce|Mix sugar, vinegar, remaining soy sauce and sesame oil. Slice ginger and scallions finely.
Fry|Heat frying oil to 160°C / 320°F. Fry separate pork slices in batches for about 4 minutes; drain. Raise oil to 200°C / 392°F and briefly re-fry about 1 minute until crisp.
Coat|Bring sauce to a simmer in a clean pan. Add ginger, scallions and fully cooked pork; toss briefly so the crust stays crisp. Serve immediately.
41: Prepare|Use a purpose-made Yunnan steam pot with a clear central chimney and matching lower pot. Cut thawed chicken into about 4 cm pieces. Mix with wine and salt; refrigerate 10 minutes.
Load|Place sliced ginger, scallion whites and chicken around the chimney. Do not add water to the inner pot or block its vents.
Steam|Fill the lower pot to its maker's level. Assemble as instructed by the maker and maintain steady steam about 90 minutes. Safely replenish the lower pot with boiling water before it runs dry.
Serve|Check thickest chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F. Add pepper and scallion greens. Use dry mitts, open the lid away from your face and serve the chicken with its condensed broth.
42: Marinate|Mix chicken with first soy sauce and wine measures, sesame oil and starch; refrigerate 20 minutes. Mix remaining soy sauces, bean paste and wine separately. Chop potatoes and peppers.
Brown|Warm oil with garlic, ginger, scallion whites, chilies, peppercorns, cumin, star anise and cassia until fragrant. Add chicken and stir-fry until lightly colored.

Braise|Add sauce and measured water. Simmer covered for 10 minutes, add potatoes and cook another 5–10 minutes, then peppers for 3–4 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F and potatoes are tender.
Serve|Cook noodles according to their package in a separate pot. Drain and top with the chicken stew and scallion greens. Remove whole spices before eating.
43: Prepare|Cut chicken thighs into 5 cm pieces and toss with soy sauce, wine and sugar. Slice ginger, halve garlic cloves and separate scallion whites from greens.
Cook aromatics|Heat cooking oil over medium-low heat with ginger, garlic and pepper flakes. Stir for 8–10 minutes until garlic is golden, not scorched.
Braise|Add chicken and its marinade. Simmer gently for 10 minutes; add scallion whites and continue 8–10 minutes, or until chicken is tender and reaches at least 74°C / 165°F.
Finish|Mix water and starch, stir into sauce and simmer about 1 minute. Remove from heat and fold in basil, sesame oil and scallion greens.
44: Prepare|Cut duck into small bone-in pieces. Chop pickled vegetables, ginger and garlic. Remove seeds from commercially preserved lemons and sour plums. Mash fermented tofu into soy sauces and wine.
Blanch and brown|Blanch duck in boiling water with some ginger and scallion, then drain. Render fatty skin in a heavy pan, adding oil only if needed. Brown duck with garlic and pickled vegetables.
Braise|Add the mixed sauce and hot water to nearly cover. Simmer gently until tender, about 30 minutes, extending until duck reaches 74°C / 165°F.
Finish|Add preserved lemon, sour plum, wampee sauce, sugar and oyster sauce near the end. Taste before adding measured salt. Reduce briefly, then fold in perilla.
45: Make filling|Finely chop cabbage, toss with salt and leave until it releases liquid; squeeze dry. Mix pork with scallions, ginger, soy sauce, wine, sesame oil and pepper, then fold in cabbage.
Wrap|Place a small spoonful of filling in each wrapper. Moisten edges with water and seal fully, keeping filling away from the seam.
Boil|Bring a wide pot of water to a gentle boil. Cook dumplings in uncrowded batches, stirring gently to prevent sticking.
Check and serve|Continue until wrappers are tender and pork centers reach 72°C / 160°F; floating alone does not prove doneness. Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve.
46: Cook rice|Bring rice and measured water to a boil, cover and simmer about 25 minutes until absorbed. Rest covered 10 minutes, fluff and spread thinly. Cool promptly; refrigerate if preparing ahead.
Prepare|Dice shrimp, mushrooms and ham. Slice scallions and beat eggs. Use ready-cooked ham.
Stir-fry|Heat oil over medium-high heat. Fry half the scallions and shrimp for 2–3 minutes. Add egg and rice, stirring to separate grains, then mushrooms, peas and ham.

Season|Add oyster sauce, sugar, salt and pepper. Toss until egg and seafood are fully cooked and the mixture is hot throughout; chilled rice must be reheated thoroughly. Finish with remaining scallions.
47: Prepare|Wash scallions, dry thoroughly and cut into thin strips. Mix light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and sugar.
Make oil|Warm cooking oil over medium heat and slowly fry scallions until golden and fragrant. Remove scallions. Lower the heat and add the sauce mixture; simmer about 2 minutes.
Cook noodles|Boil noodles according to their package until just tender. Drain well and divide among bowls.
Toss|Start with a small spoonful of sauce per bowl, toss and add more as needed to coat. Top with fried scallions. Extra sauce need not all be used.
48: Prepare|Dice tomatoes and mince garlic. Beat eggs with the tablespoon of water. Chop scallion.
Scramble|Heat four-fifths of the oil and cook the beaten eggs, stirring until set. Transfer out.
Make soup|Warm remaining oil, briefly fry garlic and add tomatoes. Cook until softened; add the 350 mL water measure and simmer 2 minutes. Add salt, sugar and eggs, cooking the egg fully.
Serve|Boil noodles separately according to package directions. Drain into bowls and pour over the tomato-egg soup. Finish with scallion.
49: Prepare|Rinse rice and soak for 30 minutes with half the oil. Peel purchased century eggs and chop. Marinate sliced pork with ginger, teaspoon of water, wine, measured salt, pepper, starch and remaining oil.
Simmer rice|Boil the four cups of water, add soaked rice and return to a simmer. Partially cover and cook 23–25 minutes, stirring occasionally and watching for overflow.
Add toppings|Stir in century egg and cook about 3 minutes. Add pork, separating the strips; simmer until fully cooked, about 3 minutes or longer as needed.
Finish|Adjust salt to taste and stir in scallion. Thin with boiling water if needed and serve carefully: thick congee stays extremely hot.
50: Make dough|Mix the main flour and salt with boiling water, then cool water. Knead about 5 minutes and rest covered 20 minutes. Mix filling flour, oil and salt into a paste; mix dipping sauce separately.
Shape|For the full batch, divide into six pieces. Roll each thin, spread with paste and chopped scallions, roll into a tube, then coil. Keep unused dough covered.
Roll|Let coils relax briefly, then flatten into thin pancakes without tearing the layers. For smaller batches, adjust the number and size of pancakes rather than making excessively thick ones.
Pan-fry|Coat a skillet with oil over medium-low heat. Cook pancakes covered initially, turning until both sides brown and the centers cook through. Cut into wedges and serve with the dipping sauce.
